critical.description: Teachers lack structured frameworks for discipline-specific instruction
critical.questionApproach: Framework-focused - teach the HOW and WHY of structured teaching

developing.description: Teachers know techniques but struggle with real-time adaptation
developing.questionApproach: Scenario-focused - teach WHEN and HOW to adjust on the fly

foundational.description: Teachers demonstrate these but inconsistently or at surface level
foundational.questionApproach: Depth-focused - deepen mastery, explore edge cases

L2.name: Comprehension Strategy Instruction
commonGaps: Models but doesn't have students practice
Skips one of the three steps (name/model/practice)
L2.trainingFocus: Teach the explicit 3-step framework for strategy instruction

L3.name: Reading-Writing Connections
commonGaps: Reading and writing taught as separate activities
No explicit verbal bridge between the two
Text not used as model for writing
L3.trainingFocus: Teach how to explicitly connect reading and writing
L3.questionFramework: FRAMEWORK - How to integrate two domains

L1.name: Explicit Phonics/Decoding
commonGaps: Jumps to blending without solid foundation
L1.trainingFocus: Teach the phonics sequence: sounds → blending → segmenting

PIA-4.name: Responsive Re-explanation
commonGaps: Repeats same explanation when students don't understand
Doesn't try different examples or analogies
PIA-4.trainingFocus: Build a toolkit of alternative explanations and examples
PIA-4.questionFramework: FRAMEWORK - Multiple ways to explain same concept

PIA-3.name: Catering to Learning Levels
PIA-3.trainingFocus: Teach differentiation: scaffold down, extend up
PIA-3.questionFramework: FRAMEWORK - How to support different learner levels

M2.name: Problem-Solving & Productive Struggle
commonGaps: Immediately gives answer when student struggles
M2.trainingFocus: Teach wait time management and productive struggle
M2.questionFramework: SCENARIO - When student struggles, what do you do?

PIA-5.name: Student Agency & Participation
commonGaps: Students are passive recipients, not active agents
PIA-5.trainingFocus: Teach how to give genuine student choice and leadership
PIA-5.questionFramework: SCENARIO - How would you give students a real choice?

M1.name: Mathematical Discourse & Reasoning
commonGaps: Doesn't ask 'why' or 'how do you know'
M1.trainingFocus: Teach how to push for mathematical reasoning
M1.questionFramework: SCENARIO - Student gives answer. What's your follow-up?

PIC-3.name: Understanding Student Misconceptions
PIC-3.trainingFocus: Teach how to detect and correct misconceptions
PIC-3.questionFramework: SCENARIO - Student has misconception. How do you respond?

PIC-4.name: Quality Questioning
PIC-4.trainingFocus: Teach how to craft and follow up with open-ended questions
PIC-4.questionFramework: REWRITE - Make these questions more open-ended

PIA-1.name: Prior Knowledge
commonGaps: Asks about prior knowledge but doesn't build on responses
PIA-1.trainingFocus: Teach how to elicit AND build on prior knowledge
PIA-1.questionFramework: SCENARIO - How would you activate and build on prior knowledge?

PIC-5.name: Effective Feedback
PIC-5.questionFramework: REWRITE - Make this feedback more specific and actionable

PIA-2.name: Meaningful Connections
commonGaps: Mentions connections but doesn't explain them
PIA-2.trainingFocus: Teach how to elaborate meaningful connections
PIA-2.questionFramework: SCENARIO - How would you connect this to student experience?

SI3.name: Subject Content Accuracy
SI3.questionFramework: SCENARIO - Handle uncertain content, verify accuracy

SI1.name: Instructional Clarity
commonGaps: Logical flow present but could be more explicit
SI1.questionFramework: REWRITE - Make this goal more specific and measurable

MA-0.name: Instructional Model Structure
MA-0.trainingFocus: Deepen I Do/We Do/You Do transitions
MA-0.questionFramework: SCENARIO - Design a lesson with clear gradual release

PIC-2.name: Use of Academic Language
PIC-2.questionFramework: SCENARIO - Model precise academic language consistently

SI2.name: Logical Flow
commonGaps: Flow exists but could be smoother
SI2.questionFramework: SCENARIO - Add smooth transitions to lesson phases

PIC-1.name: Activities & Tasks Alignment
commonGaps: Activity connected but cognitive level mismatched
Tasks present but not tightly aligned
PIC-1.questionFramework: SCENARIO - Design activities that match cognitive demand

S1.name: Inquiry-Based Approach
commonGaps: Inquiry started but gives answer too quickly
S1.questionFramework: SCENARIO - How would you extend inquiry without answering?

S2.name: Science Talk & Student Sense-Making
commonGaps: Students echo teacher language, not own words
S2.questionFramework: SCENARIO - How would you get students to explain in own words?

literacyDeficit.name: Literacy Instruction Framework Gap
literacyDeficit.rootCause: Teachers lack structured frameworks for teaching reading and writing
literacyDeficit.trainingImperative: Teach the HOW and WHY of literacy pedagogy
exampleQuestions: Design a 2-week phonics sequence starting from basics
Teach a comprehension strategy using the 3-step model
Show how you'd connect a reading assignment to a writing task

responsivenessDeficit.name: Real-Time Adaptation & Differentiation Gap
responsivenessDeficit.rootCause: Teachers don't recognize struggle signals or lack adaptation toolkit
responsivenessDeficit.trainingImperative: Teach WHEN to adapt and HOW to respond
responsivenessDeficit.questionStyle: SCENARIO - Student struggles, what's your next move?
exampleQuestions: Your student didn't understand. What's Plan B?
Show me how you'd teach this to struggling vs. advanced students
How would you handle a student who needs more wait time?
Give students a genuine choice. What would that look like?

executionInconsistency.name: High-Value Technique Inconsistency Gap
executionInconsistency.rootCause: Teachers know techniques but apply them inconsistently or shallowly
executionInconsistency.trainingImperative: Deepen consistency and quality of execution
executionInconsistency.questionStyle: REWRITE or SCENARIO - Improve the quality/consistency
exampleQuestions: Rewrite these questions to be more open-ended
A student says X. Write specific feedback, not generic praise
What follow-up would deepen this question?
How would you connect this to their prior knowledge?

foundationalStrength.name: Structural & Basic Pedagogy Mastery
foundationalStrength.rootCause: Teachers generally master these; focus on refinement
foundationalStrength.trainingImperative: Deepen mastery and extend to edge cases
exampleQuestions: In what situation might this foundational skill fail?
How would you refine this for an advanced class?
When would you break the typical structure? Why?

critical.rationale: Highest failure rates, need intensive focus on frameworks

foundational.rationale: Low failure rates, focus on depth/edge cases

foundational.focus: Extending beyond basic, edge cases, synthesis
foundational.examples: When to break the rule, why this works, exceptions
